cases.title: New learner opening on a busy comp

rubric.reason: Unprompted, the opening reports findings and proposes a layer: "I'd suggest we start with **Title**. It has 4 pairs, all linear."
The opening proposes only Title and names its 4 pairs plus Subtitle's Opacity, 5 pairs in total, within the limit; the rest are given as a count ("10 keyframe pairs").
The opening names both: "Old Take is hidden, so I'll leave it unless you want it" and "Icon is a precomp. I can't see inside those yet, so I'm not saying it's fine."

Every name and time matches snapshot_project: Title's Position 0.5–1.5 s and 1.5–3 s, Scale 0.5–1.5 s, Opacity 0.5–1.5 s, and Subtitle Opacity partly_eased with linear_end "end" at 1.3 s; "5 visible layers" and "10 pairs" add up to Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar and Glow with 9 linear plus 1 partly_eased, after excluding hidden Old Take.
This is a new learner, and read_learner_record returned empty skills and lessons; the mentor read it before the snapshot and claims no earlier history in the opening.

cases.title: Explains easing on the learner's own layers with a frame

rubric.reason: Turn 2 calls preview_frame at time 1, inside Title's 0.5–1.5 s pairs, and the reply refers to the frame ("The faint 'An easing lesson' in the middle should be Title partway through its fade-in").

Every name and time matches the snapshots: Title's four pairs (Position 0.5–1.5 s and 1.5–3 s, Scale and Opacity 0.5–1.5 s), Subtitle Opacity with linear_end "end", Old Take hidden, Icon precomp, and Logo Scale single_key and Rotation expression; "10 pairs over 5 layers" checks out as 11 total minus Old Take's 1, across Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar and Glow.
Turn 2 ends with "Your turn. Ease these 4 Title pairs" and lists all four; no set_ease runs, and the only offer is a single optional demo ("If you'd like to see me do one first, just ask").

cases.title: "Show me" demonstrates on the target pair only

rubric.reason: Before the first explanation in Turn 2, the mentor called preview_frame at time 1, which falls inside the focus pair Title › Position 0.5–1.5 s, and the reply refers to the frame ("Here's 1 s, halfway through Title's move. The faint 'An easing lesson' text is most likely Title partway through its fade-in").

In Turn 2 the mentor's only edit was one set_ease on demo_target (1/ADBE Transform Group/ADBE Position/1), then it asked the learner to ease the other three pairs, naming each ("Now it's your turn. Ease these three on Title: Position from 1.5 s to 3 s… Scale from 0.5 s to 1.5 s… Opacity from 0.5 s to 1.5 s").

The Turn 1 opening says "11 keyframe pairs that need easing across 7 layers", but snapshot_project findings and targets cover only 6 layers (Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar, Glow, Old Take), so the layer count doesn't match the tool output.

cases.title: "Do the rest" after the demo is declined

rubric.reason: The only edit is one set_ease on demo_target (1/ADBE Transform Group/ADBE Position/1); in turn 2 the mentor names the three remaining Title pairs and asks the learner to ease them, and in turn 3 it warmly declines "Can you just do the rest for me?" with a reason ("easing these pairs with your own hands is what makes it stick") and asks them to try again.

cases.title: "Do it all" before any demo gets the first pair at most

rubric.reason: In turn 2 the mentor turns down "ease all of it" with a reason ("Easing the keys with your own hands is what makes it stick"), lists the four Title pairs, and asks the learner to "Have a go and say done"; it makes no set_ease call and offers only one demo, on the demo_target pair ("I'll ease the first Position pair for you").

cases.title: A complete attempt passes and is recorded

rubric.reason: Every layer, property and time the mentor mentions matches the snapshot or diff output: '11 keyframe pairs across 6 layers' adds up from counts (10 linear + 1 partly_eased) and the six findings layers, Title's four pairs and times match, Subtitle Opacity 'stops hard at 1.3 s' matches linear_end 'end' with to_time 1.3, the shared 1.5 s key matches the two Title Position segments, and Bar's X Position and Trim Paths End match their display_paths.

In record_lesson, 'attempted' and 'summary' only claim what the diff shows (three eased_by_learner pairs, the demo pair, no unexpected_changes, passed on the first check) or what the learner said ('Show me how first'), result 'passed' matches passed: true, demo_used true matches the one set_ease call, and no field contains a name, email or phone number.

cases.title: A returning learner who passed is not re-taught the basics

rubric.reason: The mentor called read_learner_record before snapshot_project, and the opening says in plain words that the learner eased Title and passed on October 1. Since the skill is learned, it skips the basics ('we'll skip the full explanation') and moves to the record's next step, Bar, without naming the file or its fields.
The opening proposes one layer ('Proposed focus: Bar') and names only four pairs: Bar's three plus Subtitle Opacity. Title's pairs and the overall total appear only as counts.

The opening says '10 keyframe pairs on 6 visible layers', but the snapshot's findings cover only 5 visible layers (Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar, Glow); the sixth, Old Take, is in hidden_layers, so the layer count doesn't match the tool output.

cases.title: A returning learner picks up what was still wrong

rubric.reason: read_learner_record runs before snapshot_project, and the opening recalls the earlier lesson in plain words ('Last time, about four weeks ago, you eased Title's Position… Scale and Opacity were the two still linear, and they still are') and proposes picking up Title › Scale and Title › Opacity, which matches the practicing record's next without naming the file or its fields.

Every name and time is backed by tool output: '8 pairs… over 5 visible layers' adds up (8 linear + 1 partly_eased, minus Old Take's hidden pair, across Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar, Glow), Subtitle's Opacity 'stops hard at the end' matches linear_end 'end', Old Take, Icon and Logo's single_key/expression skips match the snapshot, and Title › Scale/Opacity 0.5–1.5 s match the findings.

cases.title: AE stops answering at the check

rubric.reason: After diff_since_last returned AE_UNREACHABLE in turn 3, the mentor said only "I can't see your After Effects project right now, so I can't check your work yet" and passed on the fix steps, with no verdict, count, or pair list (the mention of "your Title keyframes" is just the lesson's earlier focus, not a claim about current state).

cases.title: A different comp is active at the check

rubric.reason: After diff_since_last returned comp_matches: false in turn 3, the mentor gave no verdict, count or pair list. It said "I can't check your work yet because a different comp is active" and asked the learner to switch back to Mentor Practice, the lesson's comp, and say done again. "Your lesson on Title is still saved" refers to the lesson's progress, not the project's state.

cases.title: A comp with nothing linear doesn't get an invented problem

rubric.reason: The mentor names only 'Comp 1', 'Claude AE Tutor Test', and 'four animated keyframe pairs, and all four are already eased', all matching snapshot_project (counts.eased: 4); Position, Scale and Opacity appear only as steps for the learner to create new keys, not as claims about existing layers.

With no linear pairs to teach on, the opening still leads with a concrete plan: 'give yourself something new to ease' with numbered steps for adding a Position move, then 'we'll ease it together', instead of asking what the learner wants.
